title: GraphRAG: Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
snippet: GraphRAG extends traditional RAG by constructing a knowledge graph from source documents, enabling multi-hop reasoning across entities and relationships. Unlike flat vector retrieval, GraphRAG can answer questions requiring synthesis across multiple document chunks by traversing graph edges.

title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
snippet: Microsoft Research introduced a two-phase approach: first building a hierarchical community structure from source text using LLM-extracted entities, then using these communities to answer global queries that span the entire corpus. This contrasts with naive RAG which can only retrieve locally relevant chunks.

title: Knowledge Graph Construction for RAG Pipelines
snippet: The triple extraction phase uses LLMs to identify (subject, predicate, object) triples from text chunks. Popular approaches include few-shot prompting with GPT-4 for entity/relation extraction, followed by entity resolution to merge duplicate nodes. Quality of extraction directly impacts downstream retrieval accuracy.

title: Benchmarking RAG vs GraphRAG: When Graph Structure Helps
snippet: Empirical studies show GraphRAG outperforms flat RAG on multi-hop questions requiring 2-3 reasoning steps. However, for simple factual lookups, traditional vector RAG achieves similar quality at lower latency and cost. The sweet spot for GraphRAG is complex analytical queries over interconnected domains.

title: Multi-Agent Systems in AI Research
snippet: Multi-agent architectures decompose complex tasks into specialized sub-tasks handled by different agents. A supervisor/orchestrator pattern routes work between researchers, analysts, and writers. This approach leverages the principle of cognitive specialization — each agent optimized for a narrow responsibility.

title: Building Effective Agents: Anthropic's Design Principles
snippet: Anthropic recommends starting with the simplest solution (augmented LLM with tools) and only adding complexity when measurably justified. Key principles include: maintain agent-computer interface (ACI) quality, use structured outputs for reliability, implement guardrails for safety, and log every decision for transparency.

title: LLM Agent Guardrails and Safety Patterns
snippet: Production LLM agents require multiple safety layers: input classification (detecting harmful/out-of-scope queries), output validation (checking for hallucination and policy violations), cost caps (preventing runaway token usage), and iteration limits (stopping infinite loops). A pre-filter classifier using a cheap model like Haiku can screen queries at minimal cost.

title: LangGraph: Building Stateful Multi-Agent Applications
snippet: LangGraph provides a framework for building stateful, multi-actor applications with LLMs. It models workflows as directed graphs where nodes are agent functions and edges define routing logic. Key features include conditional branching, state persistence, and human-in-the-loop capabilities.

title: Cost Optimization Strategies for LLM Pipelines
snippet: Five strategies for reducing LLM pipeline costs: 1) Use smaller models (GPT-4o-mini, Haiku) for routine tasks, 2) Cache repeated prompts, 3) Implement token budgets per call, 4) Use structured outputs to reduce parsing overhead, 5) Batch similar requests. A well-designed multi-agent system can use model rẻ nhất while maintaining quality through architectural patterns like self-correction loops.

title: Self-Correction Loops in Agentic AI Systems
snippet: Self-correction is a key advantage of multi-agent systems: an analyst identifies gaps in research, triggers additional search, and the writer revises based on critic feedback. Studies show that 1-2 correction loops improve output quality by 15-30% on rubric-based evaluation, while more loops yield diminishing returns.

title: Comparing Single-Agent vs Multi-Agent Architectures
snippet: Single-agent architectures excel at simple, well-defined tasks with clear ground truth (factual Q&A, code generation, structured extraction). Multi-agent architectures shine when tasks require diverse skills (research + analysis + writing), iterative refinement, and quality cannot be verified automatically. The overhead of coordination (2-4x cost, 2-3x latency) must be justified by measurable quality gains.

title: Structured Output Patterns for Reliable LLM Applications
snippet: Using structured outputs (JSON mode, function calling, tool use) dramatically reduces parsing errors in production LLM applications. OpenAI's response_format parameter and Anthropic's tool-use API provide schema-validated outputs. This eliminates regex parsing and reduces hallucination in format-sensitive applications.
